title: Ginger and Egg Ribbon Sauce
description: Thin ribbons of egg white float in a glossy Cantonese-inspired ginger sauce for soft fish or chicken and rice.

ingredients.name: large egg white
ingredients.note: Separate just before cooking or use the equivalent amount of plain pasteurized liquid egg white.

steps.title: Season the broth
steps.text: Simmer {broth}, {aminos}, {ginger} and {pepper} in the HexClad for 3 minutes.

steps.title: Loosen the egg white
steps.text: Beat {white} with a fork in a small bowl just until fluid.

steps.title: Stir the slurry
steps.text: Stir {starch} into {water} in a small cup until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Bring the sauce to a simmer. Stir in the freshly mixed slurry and cook for about 1 minute, whisking until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Set the egg ribbons
steps.text: Bring the thickened base back to a gentle simmer. Stir slowly in one direction while drizzling in the egg white. Let the ribbons set for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Shorten the ribbons
steps.text: Stir for 1–2 minutes until the ribbons are opaque and the sauce reaches 160°F throughout. Break long strands into short soft flecks with the whisk.

steps.title: Finish with sesame
steps.text: Swirl in {sesame} off heat. Measure about 1 1/2 cups and add a little hot water if needed.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Spoon over fully cooked steamed fish and soft rice. Ladle the sauce around the fish as well as over the top.

notes: Yield: 1 1/2 cups. One serving is 1/4 cup. Make ahead: Make the ginger broth up to 2 days ahead and chill. Add the egg white during the final few minutes on serving day. Refrigerate in shallow covered portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: No. Egg ribbons can become spongy after freezing. For freezer prep, freeze the broth for up to 2 months and add freshly cooked ribbons after thawing. Fridge reheat: Bring a portion to a boil in a small pan, stirring until it reaches at least 165°F. Loosen with a little water as needed. Freezer reheat: Thaw in the refrigerator overnight and reheat as for a chilled portion. Option A uses ginger and white pepper. For gentler Option B, halve the ginger and omit the pepper. The sauce is dairy-free. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/6 of recipe): 16 kcal, 1.1 g protein, 2.0 g total carbohydrate, 0.4 g fat, 0.0 g fiber, 40 mg sodium. The estimate covers the prepared condiment. Add separately served foods when totaling a meal.
